name: Gareth Jiang
life: “I still remember realizing I read familiar lips before hearing the sound.” On Friday, near Tideline Market, Gareth picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I read lips in rehearsals. I offered to teach both singers without asking either for a diagnosis.
appearance: Gareth has a high puff tied with plain cord, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Gareth draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Gareth treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Gareth lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To share accessible rehearsal habits without prying.
family: Harold Crawford is Gareth’s cousin raised in the same household. Gareth picks the meeting place. Harold sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *No lifeguard at dusk*, Harold says, “I am her doctor and emphatically don't get to decide how she spends an ordinary evening.”
connections: Agnes Colón. A caption worker and monitor technician help two performers share the same rehearsal.

reactions.situation: The original singer asks to choose a seat in the audience
reactions.response: Gareth lets the singer choose a seat without alerting the whole audience.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Gareth offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.
